title: Rewrite request arbitrator and migrate regional affinity policies
creator: Maya Patel
description: The current smart routing stack contains an ad-hoc request selector (the 'policy engine') and several region-specific heuristics embedded across code paths. This has led to duplicated logic, expensive lock contention on the global route cache, brittle fallback ordering, and regular regressions when we add new regional variants. This ticket scopes a focused rewrite of the request arbitrator: extract a small deterministic arbitration core, replace inline regional affinity heuristics with a pluggable policy mesh, and migrate fallbacks to a non-blocking staged executor. Goals: reduce contention on hot code paths, make fallback ordering observable and testable, and enable safe gradual rollout of affinity changes.
technical_notes: Introduce RequestArbitrator core that evaluates candidate endpoints deterministically using a policy mesh based on priority, capacity hints, and regional affinity scores.
Replace global route lock with per-shard leases; implement optimistic reads for common-case evaluation and use evented reconciliation for updates.

Fallbacks will be moved to a staged executor: fast-pass (local/regional), retry-pass (cross-region compatible variants), and circuit-pass (lower-cost model variants). Each stage emits telemetry and traces for decision provenance.
Policy mesh config will be JSON Schema validated and versioned; we will add compatibility-tests that run policy diffs against shadow traffic before rollout.
Expected perf targets: 20-30% reduction in tail P99 latency for route selection under bursty traffic and 40% reduction in lock hold-time on the route cache under synthetic contention runs.

We will add unit tests for arbitration determinism and an integration harness that replays production traffic samples (sanitized) to validate no change in customer-visible routing unless explicitly configured.
Risks: subtle change to affinity ordering could increase egress cost if cross-region fallback frequency increases. Mitigation: shadow rollout and cost-simulation dashboard before enabling globally.
acceptance_criteria: Arbitrator module merged behind feature flag and enabled for 5% of traffic with no observable increase in 95/99 latency or request errors
Fallback stages emit structured trace IDs and metrics for each decision path (metrics documented in console-telemetry playbook)
Route cache lock hold-time reduced by at least 30% in benchmark harness compared to baseline (bench run ID linked)
All existing routing unit tests pass; new determinism tests added and stable across 1000 randomized seeds
Confluence design doc and policy schema published; rollout runbook reviewed and approved by SRE and Product
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge Refactor - land RequestArbitrator behind feature flag; disable by default; add e2e and unit tests (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/745)
Phase 1: Internal Canary - enable feature flag for internal traffic and dev tenants; collect telemetry for 72 hours; iterate on hotpath optimizations
Phase 2: Shadow Traffic - run arbitration logic in shadow mode against 10% of production requests for two weeks; compare decisions and cost impact using replay dashboard
Phase 3: Gradual Enable - enable for 5% customer traffic, monitor latency, error, and egress cost; ramp to 50% over 7 days if stable
Phase 4: Full Cutover - flip default to new arbitrator and deprecate legacy inline heuristics; remove legacy code and run dependency cleanup
